rootCause: The v1.1.5 protocol adapter recovered filePath from a nested action object but omitted the direct canonical content field, discarding valid model output.
write_file converted the missing content argument to an empty string and reported a successful zero-byte mutation.
Artifact correction did not encode mutation-required state, so the model could repeatedly inspect the already-proven empty artifact.
An oversized repeated contract, full-plan context, and expanding history consumed 702821 ms of model time for nine small action responses.
Invented external read paths were correctly blocked but recovery repeatedly delegated re-anchoring to the same model instead of inspecting the selected project root deterministically.
The model returned a nested action object whose command array was not merged into normalized run_command arguments, leaving executable absent.
The tool emitted argument_required, but the coordinator only classified argument_missing as repairable, so attempt two terminated immediately.
Three byte-identical write_file calls were journaled as real replacements, consuming mutation budget and creating unnecessary backups.
The design task had an over-broad tool allowlist and no deterministic scope validation, so an unrelated e-commerce wireframe could be treated as progress for a calculator request.
The loop detector could stop repeated inspection but could not deterministically accept a correct product artifact or redirect a no-op write to inspection.
Retry prompts did not carry forward bounded prior-attempt evidence, encouraging the model to restart with a stale absolute Git working-directory command.
The generated plan also requested system installation, a sibling project directory, and an Express backend that were unnecessary for the approved client-side calculator requirements.
The v1.1.6 path canonicalizer treated Markdown backticks surrounding a complete path scalar as literal filename characters.
The literal backtick path did not match the canonical expected artifact path, bypassing mutation-required convergence state and post-write validation.
Repeated read-only recovery and copied coordinator metadata consumed repair credits without changing durable artifact state.
A second attempt began with only two of twelve repair credits remaining and deterministically exhausted the repair budget.
